para.text: How to write an effective summary of your research
Highlight the current state of knowledge in the field.
eating a daily breakfast, preferably including products from five food groups.
Summarize either the aims of the text (i.e. this paper, essay, thesis or dissertation) or the research process (the aims, methods, findings).
The aims of this study were to examine
Recount the methodological steps in your research.
Summarize the findings/results of the study.
The percentage of participants who reported consuming breakfast every day varied
Highlight the most important implications of the research.
Health promotion efforts should aim to
(Adapted from Raaijmakers et al., 2010.) For the full reference, see References

steps.label: What is an abstract?
desc: The abstract occurs at the beginning of your dissertation or thesis. The main aim of the abstract is to provide the reader with a summary of your research.
The abstract is usually written at the end of the research process, and after writing the rest of the dissertation.

steps.label: How is it structured?
desc: The model extract is from an abstract in the field of medicine, from the ‘European Journal of Public Health’.
Abstracts in most disciplines have a combination of four moves. This extract has the four moves that most disciplines have and also includes a fifth: highlighting the implications of the research.
Here is the framework that was used to present this abstract.

steps.label: Look at Move 1
desc: The purpose of this move is to highlight the current state of knowledge in the field.

steps.label: Look at Move 2
desc: The purpose of this move is to summarize either the aims of the text (i.e. this paper, essay, thesis or dissertation) or the research process (the aims, methods, findings).

steps.label: Look at Move 3
desc: The purpose of this move is to recount the methodological steps in the research.

steps.label: Look at Move 4
desc: The purpose is to summarize the findings/results of the study.

steps.label: Look at Move 5
desc: The purpose of this move is to highlight important implications of the research.

steps.label: Show me useful language
desc: Use of the present tense, the present perfect tense or the past tense for presenting background information and presenting aims.

filters.label: It is common in the field of medicine to structure the abstract with headings.
The past tense is used to summarize the aims of the research process.
The present tense is used to provide background information.
Use of the passive voice when explaining the method.
Use of the present tense or the past tense when summarizing results. Here, the past tense is used.
Use of the modal verb ‘should’ when highlighting implications.

checkList.text: Decide on the key findings of your research.
Think about the number of moves you need for your discipline.
Decide on the most appropriate order of moves.
Make some notes and organize them into the plan.
Use academic language.
Avoid too many technical terms and lengthy references in the abstract.

Grammar Focus: providing background information
Grammar Focus: presenting the aims

Have I provided sufficient background information?

Have I summarized the results?
Have I highlighted the implications of the research, if appropriate?
